**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in TAF1 that are exclusively associated with one disease and not the other, or evidence that the functional consequences of TAF1 mutations differ significantly between the two diseases (e.g., one requiring gain-of-function and the other loss-of-function). _(variant: rs74315474)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of TAF1 in both intellectual disability and dystonia-parkinsonism could lead to the development of therapeutic strategies targeting transcriptional regulation in neuronal cells, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.

**How to falsify it:** If mutations in MRE11 are found to be completely absent in individuals with intellectual disability, X-linked, syndromic 33, or if mutations in TAF1 are not associated with DNA repair pathway dysfunction, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: Exclusion of MRE11 variants with allele frequency > 0.01 in relevant populations from causing ATLD1)_
